# Experimental Design: The Impact of QuaRot End-to-End 4-bit Quantization on Prefill and Decoding Performance of LLaMA-2 Models

**Disclaimer.** This deliverable is an *experimental design only*. No experiment has been executed, no model has been quantized or run, and no benchmark has been measured. All numerical values in this document (GPU-time estimates, memory figures, workload sizes) are planning estimates, not results.

---

## 1. Objective

To quantify how QuaRot's end-to-end 4-bit quantization (W4A4KV4) affects the **prefill** and **decoding** performance of LLaMA-2 models, and to decompose that effect into its three constituent sources: 4-bit weights, 4-bit activations, and 4-bit KV cache. The design contrasts three conditions so that each source can be isolated:

- **T0 (reference):** unquantized BF16 LLaMA-2 — baseline for quality and performance.
- **T1 (weights-only 4-bit):** W4A16KV16 — isolates the effect of 4-bit weights (memory and bandwidth), holding activations and KV cache at 16-bit.
- **T2 (end-to-end 4-bit, the QuaRot configuration under study):** W4A4KV4 — isolates the *incremental* effect of 4-bit activations and 4-bit KV cache on top of T1.

A secondary control (T3, SmoothQuant W8A8) is optional and only included if engineering time permits; it is not required to answer the research question.

## 2. Hypotheses

- **H1 (prefill throughput):** T2 achieves higher prefill tokens/s than T1 at equal batch size and sequence length, because 4-bit activations reduce compute cost in the prefill (compute-bound) regime; the delta grows with sequence length and batch size.
- **H2 (decoding latency):** T2 achieves lower per-token latency (ITL) than T0 at batch 1, because 4-bit weights reduce the memory-bandwidth cost that dominates decode; the T2-vs-T1 delta in decode is small-to-moderate since decode is weight-bandwidth-bound, not activation-compute-bound.
- **H3 (memory / KV cache):** T2 reduces peak GPU memory versus T0 proportionally to the KV-cache share, which grows with sequence length; at 8k–16k inputs the memory saving of KV4 over KV16 is large enough to increase the maximum sustainable batch size (or enable inputs that T0 cannot serve).
- **H4 (quality):** T2 incurs a small perplexity degradation relative to T0 (ΔPPL < ~0.5 on WikiText-2 for 7B/70B, per the published QuaRot findings), i.e., end-to-end 4-bit preserves most of the BF16 quality while delivering the throughput/memory gains.

## 3. Experimental Design

### 3.1 Models
- **LLaMA-2-7B** and **LLaMA-2-70B** (instruct-free base models, official checkpoints).
- LLaMA-2-13B is deliberately excluded to control cost; it is a mid-point unlikely to change the qualitative conclusions. It may be added as a robustness check only if the primary runs finish under budget.

### 3.2 Quantization configurations
| Condition | Weights | Activations | KV cache | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T0 | BF16 | BF16 | BF16 | Reference (quality + performance) |
| T1 | 4-bit (GPTQ-style, QuaRot W4A16KV16) | BF16 | BF16 | Weights-only ablation |
| T2 | 4-bit (QuaRot) | 4-bit (QuaRot, signed, with QP rotation) | 4-bit (QuaRot) | End-to-end QuaRot (primary subject) |

All T1/T2 quantization is produced with the official QuaRot repository toolchain on the same calibration set (128 sequences × 2048 tokens from C4), so differences across conditions are attributable to which tensors are quantized, not to quantization procedure.

### 3.3 Hardware and runtime
- **Hardware:** single A100-80GB for all 7B conditions; A100-80GB × 2 (tensor-parallel) for 70B. If H100 nodes are available, the design is unchanged; hardware must be fixed across all conditions within a model size.
- **Runtime:** the **QuaRot official inference harness** (HuggingFace transformers + QuaRot kernels), not vLLM, because QuaRot's A4/KV4 kernels and the W4A16KV16 path are natively supported there, keeping the three conditions directly comparable. This is a deliberate trade-off: absolute throughput numbers are not directly comparable to vLLM-based production benchmarks.
- Fixed driver/CUDA/PyTorch versions, pinned in a config file; clocks/other tenants controlled where possible (dedicated nodes, no co-tenancy).

### 3.4 Workload
- **Prompt set:** 64 fixed real-text prompts (2048 tokens each, sampled from C4/WikiText-2 with a fixed seed) for quality and end-to-end numbers, plus 32 synthetic fixed-length token streams for pure-speed measurements. Prompt order and content are frozen and logged.
- **Prefill sweep:** input lengths **{512, 1024, 2048, 4096}** × batch sizes **{1, 4, 8, 16}** (any cell exceeding the memory limit of a condition is recorded as OOM and excluded from that condition only, with the boundary reported). These ranges are set for academic benchmarking; **if the researcher has a specific production workload (different length/batch distribution), the sweep can be replaced with that workload while keeping the same metrics.**
- **Decoding sweep:** from the same prompt set, autoregressive generation of a fixed 256 output tokens at batch ∈ {1, 8}.
- **Long-context KV study (the core KV4 selling point):** input lengths 8k and 16k, batch 1 and the maximum batch that fits, comparing T0/T1 (KV16) vs T2 (KV4) on peak memory and maximum sustainable batch.

## 4. Controls

- **Within-condition controls:** identical prompts, tokenizer settings, random seeds, warm-up, and node for all conditions of a given model size; only the quantization configuration changes.
- **Between-condition controls:** T1 vs T2 differ only in activation/KV quantization; T0 vs T1 differ only in weight quantization — this is the clean three-way decomposition.
- **Calibration control:** identical calibration data and procedure for T1 and T2 (see 3.2).
- **Runtime control:** single runtime (QuaRot harness) across all conditions; no cross-runtime mixing.
- **Optional external control:** T3 (SmoothQuant W8A8) for context against a non-QuaRot scheme; excluded from the primary analysis if not completed.

## 5. Metrics and Analysis Plan

### 5.1 Metrics
- **Prefill:** time-to-first-token (TTFT) and prefill throughput (input tokens/s), per (length × batch) cell.
- **Decoding:** inter-token latency (ITL) and steady-state throughput (output tokens/s), excluding the first token; per batch.
- **Memory:** peak GPU memory per condition; KV-cache footprint reported separately (from harness-reported buffer sizes), per sequence length.
- **Quality:** per-token perplexity on WikiText-2 and C4 (same prompts, same settings across conditions); optional LAMBADA zero-shot smoke test.

### 5.2 Analysis plan
Report absolute metrics for every condition, then compute **explicit derived contrasts** so the net contribution of each quantization component is directly readable:

1. **Δ(T2 − T1) — the incremental end-to-end effect:** delta-TTFT, delta prefill throughput, delta-ITL, delta-KV-cache memory, delta peak memory. This isolates what 4-bit activations + 4-bit KV add beyond 4-bit weights.
2. **Δ(T1 − T0) — the weights-only effect:** same metric family, isolating the weight-quantization contribution.
3. **Δ(T2 − T0) — the total end-to-end effect:** the net, headline contribution of full QuaRot W4A4KV4 relative to unquantized BF16.
4. **Quality–performance joint view:** for each model size, report ΔPPL (T2 vs T0) alongside the total-effect throughput and memory deltas, so a reader can read the speed/memory gain *per unit of quality loss* directly.
5. All deltas are reported with 95% CIs (see §7) and as relative percentages; a length × batch grid of delta prefill throughput for T2 vs T1 tests the H1 trend (delta growing with sequence length).

## 6. Quality Evaluation

- **Perplexity** on WikiText-2 (test split) and C4 (fixed 2k-token windows, same as calibration-free eval set, disjoint from calibration data), computed with identical prompt construction for all conditions.
- Primary quality gate for the design: T2's ΔPPL vs T0 reported per model size; the design does not *assume* a threshold but records the value. H4's expectation (small ΔPPL) is a hypothesis to be confirmed, not a design input.
- Optional: one zero-shot task (LAMBADA) as a sanity check that perplexity and task-level behavior agree.

## 7. Statistical Protocol

- Each (condition × workload cell) is measured with **3 warm-up iterations discarded**, then **5 independent runs** (fresh process start per run to include loading effects only in a separately reported load-time metric; steady-state metrics exclude loading).
- Primary estimand per cell: mean, with a **95% confidence interval** computed by the **nonparametric bootstrap (10,000 resamples over the 5 runs)**; the bootstrap is used instead of the t-interval because n=5 is too small to assume normality of latency distributions. With n=5 the CI will be wide; this is stated as a limitation, and if wall-clock budget permits, runs may be increased to 10 to halve the CI width.
- Derived deltas (T2−T1, T1−T0, T2−T0) are computed **per run and then bootstrapped**, not from the aggregated means, so their CIs reflect run-to-run variance.
- Fixed seeds for all stochastic components; prompt order fixed; no multiple-testing correction is applied, but the document reports the full grid so readers can see the multiplicity of cells.

## 8. Feasibility and Resource Budget

- **7B (single A100-80GB):** T0/T1/T2 all fit comfortably (7B BF16 ≈ 13–14 GB weights; KV at 4k context is modest). Estimated ~1.5–2 GPU-days including quantization, calibration, and the full sweep.
- **70B — two explicit, non-ambiguous options for the BF16 reference:**
  - **(a) If two A100-80GB nodes are available:** run the **full 70B BF16 (T0) control** with tensor parallelism, including its prefill/decode sweep and perplexity; add ~2–3 GPU-days.
  - **(b) If two-GPU allocation is not available:** run 70B **only for T1 and T2**; the **quality baseline for 70B is taken from publicly published data** (the official LLaMA-2 report's WikiText-2 perplexity for LLaMA-2-70B, cited by reference), and the 7B T0 serves as the *methodological* full reference. Any comparison involving 70B "vs BF16" is then explicitly labeled as a cross-source comparison, not a same-run measurement.
  - The chosen option is fixed before the run starts and recorded in the run log; the document's results section (when produced) must state which option was used.
- **Total budget:** ≈ 4–5 GPU-days (option a) or ≈ 3–4 GPU-days (option b), plus ~2 CPU-days for harness setup and quantization calibration.
- **Known feasibility risks:** (i) QuaRot harness throughput at batch 16 for 7B may hit memory limits at 4096 context — handled by the OOM-recording rule in §3.4; (ii) 16k-context KV study for 70B BF16 may be infeasible — in that cell, T0 is replaced by its KV16 T1 counterpart and the limitation is noted.

## 9. Limitations

- **Design-only:** nothing here has been executed; all budget and memory figures are estimates.
- **Single runtime:** using the QuaRot harness (not vLLM) means absolute latency/throughput numbers are not directly comparable to production serving systems; conclusions about relative effects between T0/T1/T2 are valid, absolute serving numbers are not.
- **n=5 per cell:** bootstrap 95% CIs will be wide; small deltas (e.g., T2-vs-T1 ITL) may not be statistically resolved. Increasing to 10 runs if budget allows mitigates this.
- **70B BF16 reference may be cross-source** (option b), which weakens the 70B total-effect comparison (Δ T2−T0) for quality; performance deltas within 70B remain same-run.
- **Workload is academic:** the length/batch grid does not represent any specific production traffic (replaceable per §3.4 if the researcher supplies one).
- **No 13B point:** conclusions are for 7B and 70B; scaling behavior between sizes is interpolated, not measured.
- **Single GPU generation (A100-class):** results may shift in magnitude (not in expected direction) on H100/MI300 due to different compute-to-bandwidth ratios; the design should be re-run on a second hardware class before generalizing.
- **Calibration dependence:** T1/T2 quality depends on the fixed C4 calibration set; robustness to other calibration data is out of scope.

## 1. Objective

To quantify how QuaRot's end-to-end 4-bit quantization (W4A4KV4) affects the **prefill** and **decoding** performance of LLaMA-2 models, and to decompose that effect into its three constituent sources: 4-bit weights, 4-bit activations, and 4-bit KV cache. The design contrasts three conditions so that each source can be isolated:

- **T0 (reference):** unquantized BF16 LLaMA-2 — baseline for quality and performance.
- **T1 (weights-only 4-bit):** W4A16KV16 — isolates the effect of 4-bit weights (memory and bandwidth), holding activations and KV cache at 16-bit.
- **T2 (end-to-end 4-bit, the QuaRot configuration under study):** W4A4KV4 — isolates the *incremental* effect of 4-bit activations and 4-bit KV cache on top of T1.

A secondary control (T3, SmoothQuant W8A8) is optional and only included if engineering time permits; it is not required to answer the research question.

## 2. Hypotheses

- **H1 (prefill throughput):** T2 achieves higher prefill tokens/s than T1 at equal batch size and sequence length, because 4-bit activations reduce compute cost in the prefill (compute-bound) regime; the delta grows with sequence length and batch size.

- **H3 (memory / KV cache):** T2 reduces peak GPU memory versus T0 proportionally to the KV-cache share, which grows with sequence length; at 8k–16k inputs the memory saving of KV4 over KV16 is large enough to increase the maximum sustainable batch size (or enable inputs that T0 cannot serve).

## 3. Experimental Design

### 3.1 Models
- **LLaMA-2-7B** and **LLaMA-2-70B** (instruct-free base models, official checkpoints).

### 3.3 Hardware and runtime

- Fixed seeds for all stochastic components; prompt order fixed; no multiple-testing correction is applied, but the document reports the full grid so readers can see the multiplicity of cells.
